handbookNote: Mississippi Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Mississippi Real Estate Commission (MREC). Exam mechanics confirmed via MREC's own official PSI Candidate Information Bulletin (10/1/2023). Broker candidates must be MS residents, 21+, and (per the July 1 2026 License Law revision) either hold an active salesperson license for 12 of the previous months and complete 120 classroom hours of broker coursework (signing a 36-month no-hiring-of-salespersons affidavit under Miss. Code Ann. 73-35-7), or complete 36 months of salesperson experience first to skip that restriction; alternately, a 150-classroom-hour degree-program path. General (national) portion: 75 items (80 points, scenario items worth up to 2 pts). Mississippi state portion: 40 items (40 points). Combined: 115 items, 120 points, 4 hours (240 min). Passing score is a LITERAL PERCENT-CORRECT threshold (per MREC Rule 1.1), scored separately per section: >=75% national (60/80 points), >=80% state (32/40 points) -- notably HIGHER state-portion bar than Iowa's exam. Sections are scored separately (you can pass one and fail the other) but must both pass within the same 2-month eligibility window. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=115, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=86 (round(115*0.75)), using the national threshold as the headline figure since it's the lower of the two real per-section bars (the site's simple single-threshold scoring model can't represent two different literal percentages on one combined item count -- same category of caveat as Iowa/Oregon, but Mississippi's own thresholds ARE literal percent-correct, just two different ones per section rather than one blended figure). Mississippi has NO Real Estate Recovery Fund (confirmed absent by direct search of the current License Law -- only a 'Real Estate License Fund' under Miss. Code Ann. 73-35-19, which is MREC's own operating fund, not a consumer-recovery mechanism). NATIONAL PORTION (75 items, real PSI weights, Broker %): I. Property Ownership (10%), II. Land Use Controls (5%), III. Valuation (8%), IV. Financing (9%), V. Contracts (19%, largest section), VI. Agency (13%, incl. broker-only Supervisory Responsibilities), VII. Property Disclosures (7%), VIII. Property Management (5%, broker-only trust-fund/maintenance-responsibility/contract-provision content), IX. Transfer of Title (6%), X. Practice of Real Estate (12%, Antidiscrimination/Fair Housing/ADA/Legislation), XI. Real Estate Calculations (6%). MISSISSIPPI STATE PORTION (40 items, real Broker item counts): Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission (4), Licensing Requirements and License Maintenance (4), Property Condition Disclosures (6, incl. Miss. Code Ann. 89-1-501 et seq. and MS's real stigmatized-property carve-outs), Agency Disclosure and Duties to Parties (8, largest state section -- MS notably does NOT recognize designated/appointed agency the way some states do: MREC Rule 4.2(B) makes every salesperson a subagent of the Broker regardless of office location, so two salespeople at the same firm on opposite sides creates dual agency of the BROKER, not two separate single agencies), Advertising/Marketing/Internet (3), Out-of-State Brokers and Developers (3), Trust Accounts (3, incl. the 2026-revised 2-banking-day deposit deadline under 73-35-21(1)(f), superseding older Rule 3.4(A) 'next banking day' language), Broker Responsibilities incl. Supervision of Sales Associates (5), Records and Documents (4). Governing law: Miss. Code Ann. Title 73, Chapter 35 (73-35-1 to 73-35-35), Interest on Real Estate Brokers' Escrow Accounts Act (IREBEA, 73-35-101 to 105), MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Miss. Code Ann. 89-1-501 et seq. (Property Condition Disclosure Statement). This bank was drafted across 20 parallel single-topic drafting passes (11 national PSI sections + 9 Mississippi state-law topic groups). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
